title: Interesting Erhua
synopsis: Learn more about when and where to use the “er” sound in the Beijing dialect.

fullText.simplified:
有趣的儿化音

    京腔京味的北京话，很多人都觉得听起来特别有味道，尤其是北京话里的“儿”，一说出口就让人感觉特别亲切自然。其实，汉语里“儿化音”也不少，只不过北京话里最多。
    “儿化音”有趣，但是不能随便使用。因为有时候加了“儿”，意思就变了。比如：“头”和“头儿”，一个是身体部位，一个是领导的意思；“早点”和“早点儿”，一个是早饭的意思，一个是时间提前一些的意思；还有“他火了”和“他火儿了”，第一个是他出名了的意思，第二个是他生气了的意思。
    要是你以为只要在词后面加上一个“儿”就是北京话了，那就大错特错了！北京话里的“儿”不仅可以放在词后边，也可以放在词的中间。比如：鸭儿梨（就是我们吃的水果梨）；馅儿饼、板儿砖（砖）、事儿妈（很挑剔的人）……
    除了上边说的，再告诉你几个说好北京“儿化音”的小方法。
    来过北京的人都知道，北京带门的地名特别多，北京人说这样的地名很少加“儿”。比如东直门、前门、地安门等等，因为这些都是正式的大门。只有“西便门儿”和“东便门儿”这两个地名例外，要加“儿”。
    另外，事物小也加“儿”。比如：小碗儿、小姑娘儿、小屁孩儿等等。
    还有就是表示看不起，或者不重视的时候加“儿”。比如：这是他新来的小徒弟儿；你这么芝麻大的官儿，神气什么？
    “儿化音”很有趣，说起来却不容易。需要学习汉语的人多看多听多练习。对了，还有个好方法就是多看北京的电视节目或者电视剧。看多了慢慢就学会了！
fullText.traditional:
有趣的兒化音

    京腔京味的北京話，很多人都覺得聽起來特別有味道，尤其是北京話裡的“兒”，一說出口就讓人感覺特別親切自然。其實，漢語裡“兒化音”也不少，只不過北京話裡最多。
    “兒化音”有趣，但是不能隨便使用。因為有時候加了“兒”，意思就變了。比如：“頭”和“頭兒”，一個是身體部位，一個是領導的意思；“早點”和“早點兒”，一個是早飯的意思，一個是時間提前一些的意思；還有“他火了”和“他火兒了”，第一個是他出名了的意思，第二個是他生氣了的意思。
    要是你以為只要在詞後面加上一個“兒”就是北京話了，那就大錯特錯了！北京話裡的“兒”不僅可以放在詞後邊，也可以放在詞的中間。比如：鴨兒梨（就是我們吃的水果梨）；餡兒餅、板兒磚（磚）、事兒媽（很挑剔的人）……
    除了上邊說的，再告訴你幾個說好北京“兒化音”的小方法。
    來過北京的人都知道，北京帶門的地名特別多，北京人說這樣的地名很少加“兒”。比如東直門、前門、地安門等等，因為這些都是正式的大門。只有“西便門兒”和“東便門兒”這兩個地名例外，要加“兒”。
    另外，事物小也加“兒”。比如：小碗兒、小姑娘兒、小屁孩兒等等。
    還有就是表示看不起，或者不重視的時候加“兒”。比如：這是他新來的小徒弟兒；你這麼芝麻大的官兒，神氣什麼？
    “兒化音”很有趣，說起來卻不容易。需要學習漢語的人多看多聽多練習。對了，還有個好方法就是多看北京的電視節目或者電視劇。看多了慢慢就學會了！

sentences.traditional: 京腔京味的北京話，很多人都覺得聽起來特別有味道，尤其是北京話裡的“兒”，
sentences.pinyin: jīng qiāng jīng wèi de běi jīng huà hěn duō rén dōu jué de tīng qi lai tè bié yǒu wèi dào yóu qí shì běi jīng huà lǐ de ér

sentences.simplified: 一说出口就让人感觉特别亲切自然。
sentences.traditional: 一說出口就讓人感覺特別親切自然。
sentences.pinyin: yì shuō chū kǒu jiù ràng rén gǎn jué tè bié qīn qiè zì rán
sentences.english: Many people think that the Beijing dialect sounds very interesting, especially the “er” sound.

sentences.simplified: 其实，汉语里“儿化音”也不少，只不过北京话里最多。
sentences.traditional: 其實，漢語裡“兒化音”也不少，只不過北京話裡最多。
sentences.pinyin: qí shí hàn yǔ lǐ ér huà yīn yě bù shǎo zhǐ bu guò běi jīng huà lǐ zuì duō
sentences.english: As soon as it is spoken, it leaves a particularly familiar and natural impression.
Actually, the “er” sound is not uncommon in Mandarin Chinese, it’s just that it appears the most in the Beijing dialect.

sentences.simplified: “儿化音”有趣，但是不能随便使用。
sentences.traditional: “兒化音”有趣，但是不能隨便使用。
sentences.pinyin: ér huà yīn yǒu qù dàn shì bù néng suí biàn shǐ yòng

sentences.simplified: 因为有时候加了“儿”，意思就变了。
sentences.traditional: 因為有時候加了“兒”，意思就變了。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi yǒu shí hou jiā le ér yì si jiù biàn le
sentences.english: “Erhua” is interesting, but it can’t be used indiscriminately.

sentences.simplified: 比如：“头”和“头儿”，一个是身体部位，一个是领导的意思；
sentences.traditional: 比如：“頭”和“頭兒”，一個是身體部位，一個是領導的意思；
sentences.pinyin: bǐ rú tóu hé tóu'r yí ge shì shēn tǐ bù wèi yí ge shì lǐng dǎo de yì si
sentences.english: Because sometimes the meaning changes after adding “er”.

sentences.simplified: “早点”和“早点儿”，一个是早饭的意思，一个是时间提前一些的意思；
sentences.traditional: “早點”和“早點兒”，一個是早飯的意思，一個是時間提前一些的意思；
sentences.pinyin: zǎo diǎn hé zǎo diǎn'r yí ge shì zǎo fàn de yì si yí ge shì shí jiān tí qián yì xiē de yì si
sentences.english: Take “tou” and “tou’r” for example. The former refers to a body part, and the latter means “leader”.

sentences.simplified: 还有“他火了”和“他火儿了”，第一个是他出名了的意思，第二个是他生气了的意思。
sentences.traditional: 還有“他火了”和“他火兒了”，第一個是他出名了的意思，第二個是他生氣了的意思。
sentences.pinyin: hái yǒu tā huǒ le hé tā huǒ'r le dì yī ge shì tā chū míng le de yì si dì èr ge shì tā shēng qì le de yì si
sentences.english: As for “zaodian” and “zao dian’r”, one means “breakfast”, and the other means “earlier”.
There is also “ta huo le” and “ta huo’r le”. The former means “he became famous”, and the latter means “he’s angry”.

sentences.simplified: 要是你以为只要在词后面加上一个“儿”就是北京话了，那就大错特错了！
sentences.traditional: 要是你以為只要在詞後面加上一個“兒”就是北京話了，那就大錯特錯了！
sentences.pinyin: yào shi nǐ yǐ wéi zhǐ yào zài cí hòu miàn jiā shàng yí ge ér jiù shì běi jīng huà le nà jiù dà cuò tè cuò le

sentences.simplified: 北京话里的“儿”不仅可以放在词后边，也可以放在词的中间。
sentences.traditional: 北京話裡的“兒”不僅可以放在詞後邊，也可以放在詞的中間。
sentences.pinyin: běi jīng huà lǐ de ér bù jǐn kě yǐ fàng zài cí hòu bian yě kě yǐ fàng zài cí de zhōng jiān
sentences.english: If you think that the Beijing dialect is just adding an “er” at the end of words, then you couldn’t be more wrong!

sentences.simplified: 比如：鸭儿梨（就是我们吃的水果梨）；馅儿饼、板儿砖（砖）、事儿妈（很挑剔的人）……
sentences.traditional: 比如：鴨兒梨（就是我們吃的水果梨）；餡兒餅、板兒磚（磚）、事兒媽（很挑剔的人）……
sentences.pinyin: bǐ rú yā'r lí jiù shì wǒ men chī de shuǐ guǒ lí xiàn'r bǐng bǎn'r zhuān zhuān shì'r mā hěn tiāo ti de rén
sentences.english: In the Beijing dialect, the “er” sound isn’t just added at the end of words; it can also be put in the middle of words.
For example: “ya’rli” (the pears that we eat), “xian’rbing”, “ban’rzhuan” (brick), “shi’rma” (a fussy person) …

sentences.simplified: 除了上边说的，再告诉你几个说好北京“儿化音”的小方法。
sentences.traditional: 除了上邊說的，再告訴你幾個說好北京“兒化音”的小方法。
sentences.pinyin: chú le shàng bian shuō de zài gào su nǐ jǐ ge shuō hǎo běi jīng ér huà yīn de xiǎo fāng fǎ

sentences.english: In addition to the above, here are some tips to help you master the Beijing “erhua”.

sentences.simplified: 来过北京的人都知道，北京带门的地名特别多，
sentences.traditional: 來過北京的人都知道，北京帶門的地名特別多，
sentences.pinyin: lái guò běi jīng de rén dōu zhī dào běi jīng dài mén de dì míng tè bié duō

sentences.simplified: 北京人说这样的地名很少加“儿”。
sentences.traditional: 北京人說這樣的地名很少加“兒”。
sentences.pinyin: běi jīng rén shuō zhè yàng de dì míng hěn shǎo jiā ér
sentences.english: People who have been to Beijing will know that there are many place names in Beijing that contain the character “men”.

sentences.simplified: 比如东直门、前门、地安门等等，因为这些都是正式的大门。
sentences.traditional: 比如東直門、前門、地安門等等，因為這些都是正式的大門。
sentences.pinyin: bǐ rú dōng zhí mén qián mén dì ān mén děng děng yīn wèi zhè xiē dōu shì zhèng shì de dà mén
sentences.english: When people from Beijing say these place names, they very rarely will add the “er” sound.

sentences.simplified: 只有“西便门儿”和“东便门儿”这两个地名例外，要加“儿”。
sentences.traditional: 只有“西便門兒”和“東便門兒”這兩個地名例外，要加“兒”。
sentences.pinyin: zhǐ yǒu xī biàn mén'r hé dōng biàn mén‘r zhè liǎng ge dì míng lì wài yào jiā ér
sentences.english: For instance, Dongzhimen, Qianmen, Di’anmen, etc., because these are all official gates.
Only “Xibianmen’r” and “Dongbianmen’r” are exceptions, to which “er” should be added.

sentences.simplified: 另外，事物小也加“儿”。比如：小碗儿、小姑娘儿、小屁孩儿等等。
sentences.traditional: 另外，事物小也加“兒”。比如：小碗兒、小姑娘兒、小屁孩兒等等。
sentences.pinyin: lìng wài shì wù xiǎo yě jiā ér bǐ rú xiǎo wǎn'r xiǎo gū niang'r xiǎo pì hái'r děng děng

sentences.english: Additionally, “er” is also added to little things. For example, a small bowl, a little girl, a little tyke, etc.

sentences.simplified: 还有就是表示看不起，或者不重视的时候加“儿”。
sentences.traditional: 還有就是表示看不起，或者不重視的時候加“兒”。
sentences.pinyin: hái yǒu jiù shì biǎo shì kàn bu qǐ huò zhě bú zhòng shì de shí hou jiā ér

sentences.simplified: 比如：这是他新来的小徒弟儿；你这么芝麻大的官儿，神气什么？
sentences.traditional: 比如：這是他新來的小徒弟兒；你這麼芝麻大的官兒，神氣什麼？
sentences.pinyin: bǐ rú zhè shì tā xīn lái de xiǎo tú dì'r nǐ zhè me zhī ma dà de guān'r shén qì shén me
sentences.english: Also, “er” can be added to express disdain or indifference.
For instance: This is his new apprentice; you’re only a lowly official, why are you acting so pretentious?

sentences.simplified: “儿化音”很有趣，说起来却不容易。
sentences.traditional: “兒化音”很有趣，說起來卻不容易。
sentences.pinyin: ér huà yīn hěn yǒu qù shuō qǐ lái què bù róng yì

sentences.simplified: 需要学习汉语的人多看多听多练习。
sentences.traditional: 需要學習漢語的人多看多聽多練習。
sentences.pinyin: xū yào xué xí hàn yǔ de rén duō kàn duō tīng duō liàn xí
sentences.english: “Erhua” is very interesting, but it’s not easy to actually use in speech.

sentences.simplified: 对了，还有个好方法就是多看北京的电视节目或者电视剧。
sentences.traditional: 對了，還有個好方法就是多看北京的電視節目或者電視劇。
sentences.pinyin: duì le hái yǒu ge hǎo fāng fǎ jiù shì duō kàn běi jīng de diàn shì jié mù huò zhě diàn shì jù
sentences.english: It requires Chinese learners to watch more, listen more, and practice more.

sentences.simplified: 看多了慢慢就学会了！
sentences.traditional: 看多了慢慢就學會了！
sentences.pinyin: kàn duō le màn man jiù xué huì le
sentences.english: Oh right, another good way is to watch a lot of Beijing TV shows or dramas.
As you watch more, you’ll gradually master it!

raw.synopsis: Learn more about when and where to use the “er” sound in the Beijing dialect.
sentence_translations: Interesting Erhua
Many people think that the Beijing dialect sounds very interesting, especially the “er” sound.
As soon as it is spoken, it leaves a particularly familiar and natural impression.
Actually, the “er” sound is not uncommon in Mandarin Chinese, it’s just that it appears the most in the Beijing dialect.
“Erhua” is interesting, but it can’t be used indiscriminately.
Because sometimes the meaning changes after adding “er”.
Take “tou” and “tou’r” for example. The former refers to a body part, and the latter means “leader”.
As for “zaodian” and “zao dian’r”, one means “breakfast”, and the other means “earlier”.
There is also “ta huo le” and “ta huo’r le”. The former means “he became famous”, and the latter means “he’s angry”.
If you think that the Beijing dialect is just adding an “er” at the end of words, then you couldn’t be more wrong!
In the Beijing dialect, the “er” sound isn’t just added at the end of words; it can also be put in the middle of words.
For example: “ya’rli” (the pears that we eat), “xian’rbing”, “ban’rzhuan” (brick), “shi’rma” (a fussy person) …
In addition to the above, here are some tips to help you master the Beijing “erhua”.
People who have been to Beijing will know that there are many place names in Beijing that contain the character “men”.
When people from Beijing say these place names, they very rarely will add the “er” sound.
For instance, Dongzhimen, Qianmen, Di’anmen, etc., because these are all official gates.
Only “Xibianmen’r” and “Dongbianmen’r” are exceptions, to which “er” should be added.
Additionally, “er” is also added to little things. For example, a small bowl, a little girl, a little tyke, etc.
Also, “er” can be added to express disdain or indifference.
For instance: This is his new apprentice; you’re only a lowly official, why are you acting so pretentious?
“Erhua” is very interesting, but it’s not easy to actually use in speech.
It requires Chinese learners to watch more, listen more, and practice more.
Oh right, another good way is to watch a lot of Beijing TV shows or dramas.
As you watch more, you’ll gradually master it!
